purpose: Force the Scientific Reports 2026 closed ML-scored POSS-I cohort and JANUS open reconstructions to answer the same exposure-normalized temporal-association question before TOPA absorbs the external ML architecture as an operational component.
core_question: Is the artifact-score-weighted POSS-I candidate rate per actual observing opportunity higher on nights falling inside the same frozen nuclear-test window than outside it, and does that effect survive the same statistic in both closed and open cohorts?

study_window.window_definition: +/- 1 calendar day around each event in the frozen nuclear manifest

primary_estimand.candidate_level_score: s_i = raw artifact-realness score in [0,1]; it is a model score, not assumed calibrated probability
primary_estimand.nightly_weighted_outcome: Y_d = sum_i(s_i) for candidates observed on date d
primary_estimand.nightly_opportunity: O_d = frozen usable observing opportunity for date d, expressed in the same denominator within a cohort (tiles, usable patches, or usable imaged area) and reconciled before cross-cohort interpretation
primary_estimand.exposed_rate: R_E = sum_{d in nuclear_window}(Y_d) / sum_{d in nuclear_window}(O_d)
primary_estimand.unexposed_rate: R_U = sum_{d outside nuclear_window}(Y_d) / sum_{d outside nuclear_window}(O_d)

primary_null.test: Compare observed RR_score to every valid circular shift of the frozen nuclear calendar across the full study window.
primary_null.primary_p: one-sided exact upper-tail fraction with RR_shift >= RR_observed
primary_null.secondary_p: two-sided log-distance from the null median

same_for_all_cohorts: score semantics: raw score != calibrated probability
opportunity_reconciliation: Document exactly what one opportunity unit means in every cohort.
Do not equate candidate count with observing opportunity.
Do not use ANY_CANDIDATE as an outcome when every observed night is candidate-positive.

If closed and open opportunity units cannot be made commensurate, run identical within-cohort rate ratios and a common-observed-date intersection analysis; do not pool raw denominators across incompatible units.
mandatory_harmonization.common_date_intersection: Mandatory secondary replay on dates observed in every supplied cohort.

collapse_guard: Every candidate keeps its original raw score even if a calibrator is later added.
Calibration diagnostics are evaluated independently of the nuclear association.
If a calibrator collapses the score distribution, its output may be retained for audit but cannot become the sole weighted outcome.
No calibrator is selected because it strengthens the nuclear-window p-value.

secondary_outcomes.role: Direct bridge to JPFM-2E and independent open reconstructions.

secondary_outcomes.definition: count of candidates with raw score >= a threshold frozen from training/OOF behavior before nuclear testing, divided by opportunity
secondary_outcomes.guard: Threshold must not be selected on nuclear-window significance.

secondary_outcomes.definition: Repeat all primary/secondary statistics on the intersection of observation dates across cohorts.

must_wait_until_harmonization: treating the external classifier as TOPA's canonical POSS-I artifact judge
treating its nuclear-window result as a prior probability of the nuclear hypothesis
using its raw score as a calibrated physical probability
future_training_guards: group CV by plate and/or observation date when same-plate leakage is possible
nuclear labels excluded from features, split construction and hyperparameter selection
raw score, rank and any calibrated sidecar all exported separately
negative controls and artifact-rich holdouts required

cross_cohort_decision_rule.strengthen: If RR_score > 1 with p_upper <= 0.05 under the same primary test in both closed and open cohorts, the effect has compatible direction, and the common-date intersection does not reverse the sign, classify as HARMONIZED_REPLICATION_SIGNAL. This strengthens a temporal association only.
cross_cohort_decision_rule.destroy_general_claim: If the apparent effect disappears under shared opportunity normalization, reverses direction, or survives only in one cohort, classify it as DATASET_OR_PIPELINE_SPECIFIC and do not promote a general POSS-I/nuclear-window association.
cross_cohort_decision_rule.mixed: Conflicting but valid cohort results remain UNRESOLVED; TOPA does not average them into a preferred story.
cross_cohort_decision_rule.causation: No result from this experiment alone can establish nuclear causation, UAP origin, NHI, or the historical global resonance field.

janus_open_jpfm_2e.known_summary: 122511 candidates, 312 observed nights, 31360 tiles; opportunity-normalized positive nuclear rate not established in JPFM-2E.

scientific_reports_2026_closed.known_summary: Closed 107875-candidate ML-scored cohort reports residual nuclear-window association within its own analysis design.
scientific_reports_2026_closed.blocker: TOPA cannot honestly execute the same byte-level harmonization until the closed candidate rows/scores and a compatible observing-opportunity manifest are available or independently reconstructed.

common_nuclear_manifest.requirement: Freeze one exact event manifest byte-for-byte before first real harmonized run. Paper-matching DOE above-ground dates should be the primary replay arm; other calendars may be preregistered as secondary arms rather than substituted afterward.

expected_output.format: JSON receipt plus optional JSONL/NDJSON row-level derivatives
expected_output.required_status: EXECUTED_ON_SUPPLIED_COHORTS or explicit BLOCKED status; never simulated as real data.
